turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Ujakalashe olambileyo. Kudala-dala kwakukho usapho olwaluhlala efama. Kwakukho nojakalashe owayelambe kakhulu, engenakutya.
turns.en: The hungry jackal. Long, long ago there was a family that lived on a farm. There was also a jackal who was very hungry, having no food.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: wayelambe kakhulu, engenakutya. Wahamba-hamba ekhangela ukutya. Wabona abantwana abazidlalelayo. Wabaleqa abo bantwana.
turns.en: he was very hungry, having no food. He walked around looking for food. He saw children playing by themselves. He chased those children.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Bayongena emakhayeni abo, baxelela oomama babo abo bantwana. Babekoyika uDakalashi.
turns.en: They went into their homes, those children told their mothers. They were afraid of Jackal.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Ngentsasa elandelayo bavuka baya edolophini. Xa bephuma babona uDakalashi ehleli phantsi komthi omkhulu.
turns.en: The following morning they woke up and went to town. When they went out they saw Jackal sitting under a big tree.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.en: A spider is not an insect.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.en: It is not a- it is not an insect.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.en: It is not it is not an insect.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: Please read again where it was written.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: A spider does not have wings. A spider eats insects.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Makhe siqale msinyane ke. Zeziphi ezi nambuzane esidibene nazo? Siqale sadibana nantoni?
turns.en: Let us start quickly then. Which are these insects we have met? First we met what?

turns.speaker: Learners
turns.en: Which lives next to the water.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: Which lives next to the water.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.en: Which has a red colour and red and black colours.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: Which has a red colour and black spots.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: What does the butterfly of the legend do?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Ndiqokelele incindi. Good boy. Sadibana nantoni?
turns.en: I collect nectar. Good boy. We met what?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Iqritsi. Kuthiwa yintoni kaloku mgama lale sixhosa? Yinyendane. Yenza ntoni yona?
turns.en: A cricket. What is it called again in this Xhosa language? It is a cricket. What does it do?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Intsusu, isikhwazi. Thetha kakuhle. Sadibana nantoni?
turns.en: A cicada, a cicada. Speak well. We met what?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Nembovane. Imbovane yona kuthiwa itheni? Iyathanda ukusebenza. Ikhuthele. Good. Iyathanda ukusebenza.
turns.en: With an ant. The ant, what is said about it? It likes to work. It is active. Good. It likes to work.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Kuthiwa isigcawu sona sithini? Asosinambuzane. Senzantoni isigcawu? Sitya intoni?
turns.en: What is said about the spider itself? It is not an insect. What does a spider do? What does it eat?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Sitya iintoni? Izinambuzane. Nifunde kakuhle kakhulu okumeke abantwana bam.
turns.en: What does it eat? Insects. You read very well indeed, my children.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Buyelani ezidesikeni ke, sikhuphe la mbongo.
turns.en: Go back to the desks then, so we can take out that poem.
